thinkingSteps.body: For “Binary Search”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = 9 should still produce 4.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: Binary search is an efficient technique to search for a target element in a sorted array. In each step, we compare the middle element of the array with the target. If the middle element is equal to the target, we have found the element and return its index. If the middle element is greater than the target, we narrow down the search to the left half of the array. If the middle element is smaller, we narrow down the search to the right half of the array. We repeat this process until we find the target element or the search space is exhausted.
